title: Career Roadmap · Site Assistant
summary: A Site Assistant supports construction-site operations by helping with measurements, materials, work records, drawing coordination, safety checks and communication between supervisors, contractors and workers.

blocks.label: Recommended
blocks.text: Class 10 for relevant ITI routes; Class 12 can broaden further-study options.

blocks.label: Stream
blocks.text: Science with Mathematics is useful for technical progression, but is not mandatory for every entry-level site-support job.

blocks.label: Explore
blocks.text: Construction methods, site measurements, drawings, materials and safety practices.

blocks.label: Early skills
blocks.text: Basic arithmetic, communication, teamwork, observation and safe work habits.

blocks.label: Stage 1 — Foundation
blocks.text: Construction terminology, basic measurements, site layout and drawing interpretation.

blocks.label: Stage 2 — Core skills
blocks.text: Material tracking, measurement records, daily progress logs and assisting supervisors.

blocks.label: Stage 3 — Advanced skills
blocks.text: Quantity take-offs, basic CAD drawings, quality checklists and work scheduling.

blocks.label: Stage 4 — Job preparation
blocks.text: Maintain sample site reports, practise safety procedures and learn site documentation workflows.

blocks.label: Project ideas
blocks.text: Daily site-progress report • Material stock register • Simple quantity-estimation sheet • Site safety inspection checklist.

CAD or quantity-estimation training for technical progression.

blocks.text: A certificate does not replace supervised site experience or any qualifications required for regulated duties.

blocks.text: Academic records, language proficiency where applicable, course prerequisites and practical experience for some programs. Verify international-student eligibility and current course details on official websites.
